zh.text: 如果雨滴跟棒球一樣大？
直徑七點四公分。
真正的雨滴，大約只有兩毫米。
五萬顆，才裝得滿一顆棒球雨滴。
一顆大約兩百一十克，
比一顆棒球還重。
落地時速大約一百五十公里，
跟職棒快速球差不多。
換成一場普通的中雨，
每秒有四十七顆，砸在一座足球場上。
但這不可能。
雨滴根本不是淚滴形：
小的是圓球，兩三毫米就像漢堡麵包。
到了五毫米，空氣把它吹成降落傘——
zh.say: 到了五毫米，空氣把它吹成降落傘，

zh.text: 然後啪，碎了。
空氣贏過了表面張力。
天上真的會掉棒球大的東西：冰雹。
冰撐得住，水撐不住。
落下不到一公尺，就碎成一場小雨。
所以放心，出門不用戴打擊頭盔。

en.text: What if raindrops were as big as baseballs?
7.4 centimeters across.
A real raindrop is about 2 millimeters.
It takes 50,000 of them to fill one baseball-sized drop.
One would weigh about 210 grams,
heavier than a baseball.
It would land at about 150 kilometers an hour,
as fast as a pro fastball.
Now, an ordinary moderate rain:
47 of them every second, on a single football pitch.
But it can't happen.
Raindrops aren't even teardrop-shaped.
Small ones are round. Bigger ones look like a burger bun.
At about 5 millimeters, air puffs it into a parachute,
and it bursts.
Air pressure beats surface tension.
The sky does drop baseball-sized things: hail.
Ice holds together. Water can't.
Within 1 meter, it bursts into rain.
So relax. No batting helmet needed.
